I farm only 5 mu, and cotton is the crop I know best after 35 years, so I will keep the whole field in cotton this year instead of changing crops. Because my land is small and I have well irrigation, I will manage for stability rather than gamble on a low-input crop. I will use improved seed, not traditional seed, because I care more about steady emergence, boll setting, and cleaner picking than saving a little on seed. At the start of the season I will prepare the land with rotary tillage since it is efficient on a small plot and fits my labor situation. For fertilizer, I will put in a moderate but not excessive amount: enough nitrogen to support vegetative growth, phosphorus to help rooting and early growth, and potassium to support boll development and plant strength. Since I have irrigation from a well, I will plan several waterings around the main demand periods instead of depending on rainfall. I will also spray pesticides a few times, because in cotton I do not like waiting until pests spread. My goal is a steady, manageable crop with decent yield, not the highest possible yield with higher cost and risk.
